papers.title: Circuit Mechanisms for Spatial Relation Generation in Diffusion Transformers
papers.status: CVPR 2026 verified via official CVF proceedings
papers.models: PixArt-style DiT B/mini/micro/nano trained from scratch on two-shape tasks with RTE/T5/CLIP; limited pretrained PixArt-Sigma analysis
papers.interventions: Token and attention-head ablation; QK/VO circuit manipulation; factor-vector arithmetic on T5 object-token embeddings
papers.scores: Geometric shape/color/binding and strict/loose relation binary correctness; generated-object masks; relation head alignment
findings: Attention Synopsis aggregates category-specific attention over layers/heads/time and reveals sparse circuits.

RTE relation/shape heads operate in sequence; contextual T5 tokens mix object and relation information; manipulating relation factors changes relation while preserving shape/color in the illustrated controlled setup.
A head-screening procedure uses fixed position embeddings and text factors with QK weights without image generation, followed by causal validation.
papers.overlap: Direct visualization-to-hypothesis-to-intervention mechanism discovery, multi-fact outputs and a cheaper localization heuristic already exist. Not same-instance safe repair routing between encoder and denoiser.
limitations: Main mechanistic conclusions from simple self-trained models and factorial prompts.
Pretrained test selects a highest-performing prompt after only8/30 object pairs show nontrivial capability; not broad recovery evidence.
Weight screening assumes positional embedding dominates query spatial structure and requires causal ablation.
Ablation effect and controllability do not establish a unique original failure source.

papers.title: SCOPE: Structured Decomposition and Conditional Skill Orchestration for Complex Image Generation
papers.status: 2026 arXiv preprint; formal acceptance not checked

papers.interventions: Commitment-based verification routes to retrieval/reasoning, prompt rewriting, local image editing or regeneration, at most3 generation attempts
papers.scores: Entity-Gated Intent Pass Rate (all required entities and constraints), item-level entity/gated-constraint pass; WISE-V/MindBench
findings: Explicitly retains entities, attributes, relations, layout and unresolved requirements across generation and repair.

Equal generation counts do not match all model calls, search and wall time.
Verifier errors can propagate; no internal fault-source ground truth or dedicated original-correct-fact retention endpoint.

papers.title: The Plan, Not the Decoder: Diagnosing and Repairing Compositional Failure in Reasoning-Augmented Text-to-Image Generation
papers.status: arXiv claims ECCV2026 oral; official acceptance not independently verified
papers.models: GoT-R1-1B/7B (Janus-Pro family): explicit object/attribute/box plan before autoregressive image-token generation; not FLUX/diffusion text-encoder patching
papers.interventions: Box and color swaps, chain ablation, object-segment order change; symbolic plan verification/rejection sampling; minimal/geometric plan repair and external plan replacement
papers.scores: OWLv2 object centers/IoU and prompt-vs-plan relation correctness; BLIP color questions; paired permutation tests and human metric validation
findings: Control generated-layout plan fidelity93.8%; a correct generated image is separate from a faithfully executed but incorrect plan.
Table1,p6: verification+5.0pp, minimal repair+6.0pp, geometry repair+10.7pp relative to specified path-matched controls on300 spatial prompts.
Bulk attention to box tokens about0.7%, weak control r=.17 and near0 elsewhere; does not explain repair.
7B repair gains1.7–2.3pp individually nonsignificant; only full clean-box replacement+6.3pp significant.
papers.overlap: Direct component diagnosis through counterfactual interventions followed by cheaper upstream repair already exists. Checkable textual plans make cheap symbolic checks possible; not proof of unique fault identification in opaque FLUX embeddings.
limitations: One model family and300-prompt validation subsets; main spatial outcomes not all-fact preservation.
Color verifier checks presence not binding; donor chains can retain mismatched prose.
Older cross-family encoder probes predate audited pipeline and are context-only; should not support quantitative encoder claims.

assessment.verdict: Conditional small pilot only; not yet a preferred paper commitment. No existing paired demonstration found here that encoder and denoiser actions have complementary safe-success sets on the same natural error family.
assessment.identifiable: Fixed-action intervention effects under controlled model/prompt/noise; not unique component fault origins. Explicit readable plan correctness is unavailable for opaque FLUX embeddings.
assessment.insertion: After first failed image with recorded internal trajectory, before repair replay; use cheap original-trace features or strictly budgeted partial intervention probes, predict unexecuted action final facts.
strongest_baselines: same-total-cost direct candidate generation plus identical output factual verifier
offline whole-menu oracle only as opportunity estimate
fatal_risks: E+D operates within one denoising run and may dominate without meaningful extra cost.
If diagnostic probes fully generate all candidates, they add no outcome information beyond direct search.
Cross-dataset lexical-vs-visual leakage routing can disguise trivial task-type recognition.
No verified cheap internal signal reliably predicts target and original-correct facts across full denoising trajectory.
assessment.root_current_candidate_comment: For identity enhancement / cross-entity suppression / joint / no-op within the same denoiser, attribution can only beat direct trials through cheaper reliable prediction of untried results or better information per probe. Let trial baseline directly deliver any already-generated successful candidate; do not force a redundant replay. DeLeaker degraded-rate is not established relation-damage rate.
